lifecycle.content:
name: homebrew
version: "4.4.11"
description: The Missing Package Manager for macOS (or Linux)
homepage: https://brew.sh
repository: https://github.com/Homebrew/brew
license: BSD-2-Clause

authors:
  - name: Max Howell
    url: https://github.com/mxcl
  - name: Homebrew maintainers
    url: https://github.com/orgs/Homebrew/people

platforms:
  - darwin
  - linux

features:
  analytics:
    description: Enable anonymous usage analytics
    default: true

settings:
  homebrew_prefix:
    type: string
    description: Installation prefix (auto-detected based on architecture)
    default: ""
  
  homebrew_no_install_cleanup:
    type: boolean
    description: Retain old formula versions after upgrade
    default: false
    
  homebrew_no_analytics:
    type: boolean
    description: Disable analytics collection
    default: false

dependencies: []
conflicts: []

phases:
  prepare: prepare.star
  install: install.star
  provision: provision.star
  verify: verify.star

verification:
  command: "brew --version"
  pattern: "Homebrew"

tags:
  - package-manager
  - macos
  - linux
  - cli

prepare.content:
# homebrew/prepare.star - Prepare phase for Homebrew
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# Homebrew requires Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS. Without CLT,
# the installer will prompt interactively, breaking automation.
# We check for CLT first and install if missing.
#
# On Linux, build dependencies must be installed or Homebrew will
# fall back to building everything from source (very slow).

def prepare():
    """Check preconditions and install dependencies."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _prepare_darwin()
    elif platform.os == "linux":
        _prepare_linux()
    return {"prepare": True}

def _prepare_darwin():
    """Ensure Xcode Command Line Tools are installed."""
    # Check if CLT already installed
    result = shell.exec(
        "xcode-select -p",
        allowed_commands=["xcode-select"],
    )
    
    if not result.success:
        # Install Command Line Tools
        shell.exec(
            "xcode-select --install",
            allowed_commands=["xcode-select"],
        )
        
        # Accept license if needed
        shell.exec(
            "sudo xcodebuild -license accept",
            allowed_commands=["xcodebuild"],
        )

def _prepare_linux():
    """Install build dependencies for Linux."""
    if platform.distro in ["ubuntu", "debian"]:
        # Update package list first
        shell.exec(
            "sudo apt-get update",
            allowed_commands=["apt-get"],
        )
        
        # Install build essentials
        package.install([
            "build-essential",
            "procps",
            "curl",
            "file",
            "git"
        ], manager="apt")
        
    elif platform.distro in ["fedora", "rhel", "centos"]:
        # Install development tools group
        shell.exec(
            "sudo dnf group install 'Development Tools'",
            allowed_commands=["dnf"],
        )
        
        package.install([
            "procps-ng",
            "curl",
            "file"
        ], manager="dnf")
        
    elif platform.distro == "arch":
        package.install([
            "base-devel",
            "procps-ng",
            "curl",
            "file",
            "git"
        ], manager="pacman")

def rollback():
    """No rollback needed for prepare phase."""
    pass

install.content:
# homebrew/install.star - Install phase for Homebrew
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# Homebrew uses architecture-specific install paths:
# - Apple Silicon (arm64): /opt/homebrew
# - Intel (x86_64): /usr/local
# - Linux: /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew
#
# The official installer script handles all platform detection
# and path logic automatically. We use it rather than reimplementing.

INSTALL_SCRIPT_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh"
UNINSTALL_SCRIPT_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/uninstall.sh"

def install():
    """Install Homebrew using official installer script."""
    # Set noninteractive mode to prevent prompts
    env.set("NONINTERACTIVE", "1")
    
    # Download and execute installer script
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE: Using /bin/bash ensures compatibility
    # with both macOS (which has old bash) and Linux systems
    shell.exec(
        f'/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL {INSTALL_SCRIPT_URL})"',
        allowed_commands=["bash", "curl"],
    )
    
    return {"install": True}

def _get_homebrew_prefix():
    """Get the correct Homebrew prefix for this platform/architecture."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        if platform.arch == "arm64":
            return "/opt/homebrew"
        else:
            return "/usr/local"
    elif platform.os == "linux":
        return "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"
    else:
        fail(f"Unsupported platform: {platform.os}")

def rollback():
    """Uninstall Homebrew using official uninstall script."""
    # Set noninteractive mode for automated uninstall
    env.set("NONINTERACTIVE", "1")
    
    # Use official uninstaller
    shell.exec(
        f'/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL {UNINSTALL_SCRIPT_URL})"',
        allowed_commands=["bash", "curl"],
    )

provision.content:
# homebrew/provision.star - Provision phase for Homebrew
#
# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# After Homebrew installs, it's not automatically in PATH.
# Users must add `eval "$(brew shellenv)"` to their shell profile.
# This is the #1 source of "brew command not found" issues.
#
# We detect the shell and add the appropriate configuration.

def provision():
    """Configure Homebrew in user's shell environment."""
    _setup_shell_environment()
    _initial_update()
    _configure_analytics()
    return {"provision": True}

def _setup_shell_environment():
    """Add Homebrew to shell PATH configuration."""
    homebrew_prefix = _get_homebrew_prefix()
    shell_env_command = f'eval "$({homebrew_prefix}/bin/brew shellenv)"'
    
    # Detect user's shell
    shell_name = env.get("SHELL", "/bin/bash").split("/")[-1]
    
    # Add to appropriate shell config file
    if shell_name == "zsh":
        config_file = env.expand("~/.zshrc")
    elif shell_name == "bash":
        if platform.os == "darwin":
            config_file = env.expand("~/.bash_profile")
        else:
            config_file = env.expand("~/.bashrc")
    elif shell_name == "fish":
        # Fish uses different syntax
        config_file = env.expand("~/.config/fish/config.fish")
        shell_env_command = f'{homebrew_prefix}/bin/brew shellenv | source'
    else:
        # Default to .profile for unknown shells
        config_file = env.expand("~/.profile")
    
    # Check if already configured
    if fs.exists(config_file):
        content = fs.read(config_file)
        if "brew shellenv" in content:
            return  # Already configured
    
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE: We append to the file rather than prepend
    # because some shell configs have early returns that would
    # skip our PATH modification
    fs.write(
        config_file,
        f"\n# Added by Homebrew installer\n{shell_env_command}\n",
        append=True
    )

def _initial_update():
    """Perform initial Homebrew update to sync repositories."""
    homebrew_prefix = _get_homebrew_prefix()
    brew_path = f"{homebrew_prefix}/bin/brew"
    
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE: First brew update after install is critical
    # It syncs the local tap repositories with upstream, enabling
    # formula installations
    shell.exec(
        f"{brew_path} update",
        allowed_commands=["brew"],
    )

def _configure_analytics():
    """Configure analytics based on user preference."""
    homebrew_prefix = _get_homebrew_prefix()
    brew_path = f"{homebrew_prefix}/bin/brew"
    
    # Check feature setting
    analytics_enabled = env.get("LORE_FEATURE_ANALYTICS", "true") == "true"
    
    if not analytics_enabled:
        shell.exec(
            f"{brew_path} analytics off",
            allowed_commands=["brew"],
        )

def _get_homebrew_prefix():
    """Get the correct Homebrew prefix for this platform/architecture."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        if platform.arch == "arm64":
            return "/opt/homebrew"
        else:
            return "/usr/local"
    elif platform.os == "linux":
        return "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"
    else:
        fail(f"Unsupported platform: {platform.os}")

def rollback():
    """Remove Homebrew shell configuration."""
    # Remove shell environment setup from config files
    config_files = [
        env.expand("~/.zshrc"),
        env.expand("~/.bash_profile"),
        env.expand("~/.bashrc"),
        env.expand("~/.profile"),
        env.expand("~/.config/fish/config.fish"),
    ]
    
    for config_file in config_files:
        if fs.exists(config_file):
            content = fs.read(config_file)
            # Remove Homebrew-related lines
            lines = content.split("\n")
            filtered_lines = []
            skip_next = False
            
            for line in lines:
                if "Added by Homebrew installer" in line:
                    skip_next = True
                    continue
                if skip_next and "brew shellenv" in line:
                    skip_next = False
                    continue
                filtered_lines.append(line)
            
            fs.write(config_file, "\n".join(filtered_lines))

readme.content:
# Homebrew

Homebrew is "The Missing Package Manager for macOS (or Linux)". It installs the stuff you need that Apple (or your Linux system) didn't install by default. Homebrew makes it easy to install command-line tools, applications, fonts, and more.

## Features

| Feature | Description | Default |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| analytics | Enable anonymous usage analytics | `true` |

## Settings

| Setting | Type | Description | Default |
|---------|------|-------------|--------|
| homebrew_prefix | string | Installation prefix (auto-detected based on architecture) | `""` |
| homebrew_no_install_cleanup | boolean | Retain old formula versions after upgrade | `false` |
| homebrew_no_analytics | boolean | Disable analytics collection | `false` |

## Platform Support

- **macOS**: Full support on both Intel and Apple Silicon
  - Apple Silicon (arm64): Installs to `/opt/homebrew`
  - Intel (x86_64): Installs to `/usr/local`
- **Linux**: Supported on major distributions
  - Installs to `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`
  - Requires build dependencies (automatically installed)

## Tribal Knowledge

### Architecture-Specific Install Paths
*Reference: install.star:41-50*

Homebrew uses different installation prefixes based on your Mac's architecture:
- Apple Silicon Macs: `/opt/homebrew` 
- Intel Macs: `/usr/local`
- Linux: `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`

This matters because the PATH configuration is different for each. The package automatically detects your architecture and configures the correct path.

### Shell Configuration Required
*Reference: provision.star:15-55*

After installation, Homebrew is not automatically in your PATH. You must add `eval "$(brew shellenv)"` to your shell profile. This is the #1 cause of "brew command not found" errors. The package automatically adds this to your shell configuration file based on your current shell (zsh, bash, fish).

### Command Line Tools Dependency
*Reference: prepare.star:10-35*

On macOS, Homebrew requires Xcode Command Line Tools. Without CLT, the installer will prompt interactively, breaking automation. The package checks for and installs CLT before running the Homebrew installer.

### First Update Is Critical
*Reference: provision.star:70-78*

After installation, you must run `brew update` to sync local tap repositories with upstream. Without this, formula installations will fail. The package automatically performs this initial update.

### OS Upgrade Considerations

After macOS upgrades:
1. Update Xcode Command Line Tools: `xcode-select --install`
2. Accept Xcode license: `sudo xcodebuild -license accept`  
3. Update Homebrew: `brew update`
4. Fix permissions if needed: `sudo chown -R $(whoami) $(brew --prefix)/*`

### Linux Build Dependencies
*Reference: prepare.star:45-85*

On Linux, Homebrew needs build tools to compile packages from source when prebuilt "bottles" aren't available. The package installs the appropriate development tools for your distribution (build-essential on Ubuntu/Debian, Development Tools on RHEL/Fedora, base-devel on Arch).

## Sources

- [Homebrew Homepage](https://brew.sh) - Official website and documentation
- [Installation Documentation](https://docs.brew.sh/Installation) - Official install guide
- [Homebrew on Linux](https://docs.brew.sh/Homebrew-on-Linux) - Linux-specific installation
- [FAQ and Troubleshooting](https://docs.brew.sh/FAQ) - Common issues and solutions
- [Install Scripts Repository](https://github.com/Homebrew/install) - Official installer/uninstaller scripts
